headline.text: Credit is growing at 12.9% y/y against deposit growth of 6.5%, lifting the loan-to-deposit ratio 4.3 pp to 76.8%. Overdue balances are up AZN 194 mln y/y to 2.1% of loans while the bank NPL ratio is broadly stable at 2.9%. The Central Bank held its rate at 6.50% on 31 July but changed its reasoning, and its July round now projects 6.1% inflation at end-2026.

statement.text: Loans grew 12.9% y/y against 6.5% for deposits, a gap of about six percentage points that has lifted the loan-to-deposit ratio 4.3 pp to 76.8%. The funding side is carried entirely by households, up 15.8% y/y, while corporate deposits fell 4.3%.

banking_relevance.text: A sector funding gap of this size is where deposit competition starts. New AZN term deposits already price at 7.5%, 0.4 pp higher than a year ago, while the new-lending rate is 19.0% and the indicative spread has narrowed 0.4 pp to 11.5 pp.

caveat.text: The loan-to-deposit ratio here is gross loans over deposits for all credit institutions. It is not a regulatory liquidity ratio and says nothing about any individual bank's funding position.

statement.text: Overdue loans across all credit institutions rose AZN 194 mln over the year to 2.1% of the portfolio, 0.4 pp higher than a year earlier. The prudential NPL ratio for banks moved far less, to 2.9% from a balance of AZN 932 mln.

banking_relevance.text: Balances are deteriorating faster than ratios because the denominator is growing quickly. A stable ratio on a fast-growing book is not the same as stable asset quality, and the difference shows up first in arrears data that only the bank itself holds.

caveat.text: Overdue loans and non-performing loans are different published concepts with different populations. Neither series establishes new formation as against slower write-offs.

statement.text: The Central Bank left the refinancing rate at 6.50% on 31 July, with the corridor at 5.50% to 7.50%, while its stated reasoning changed between the June and July decisions. It says: \u201cRisks to the inflation outlook remain tilted to the upside\u201d.

quotes.text: Risks to the inflation outlook remain tilted to the upside

banking_relevance.text: An unchanged corridor with a changed rationale is a different signal from an unchanged corridor with an unchanged one: it says the conditions under which the next move happens have moved, not the price of money today. The Bank adds that its decisions \u201cwill remain data-dependent\u201d.

caveat.text: The stance label describes the rate decision only. Nothing in the decision text indicates an intermeeting move, and the next decision is scheduled.

statement.text: Actual inflation was 5.7% in August, but the Central Bank's July round projects 6.1% at end-2026 and 5.8% at end-2027, with non-oil growth of 2.4% this year. It states: \u201cThe Central Bank forecasts that annual inflation will remain within the target range in the medium run\u201d.

quotes.text: The Central Bank forecasts that annual inflation will remain within the target range in the medium run

banking_relevance.text: A projected path above today's outturn argues against assuming that deposit pricing pressure fades on its own. It is the Bank's projection, not an outcome and not our own scenario.

caveat.text: Projections are published for named target periods. The August 2026 round states no comparable target that the May round also published, so no like-for-like revision can be computed here.

statement.text: Regulatory capital adequacy for the sector was 17.6% and the liquidity coverage ratio 154.0% at end-December 2025, published in April 2026. Under the Bank's published adverse scenario, capital adequacy is projected at 13.6% by 2027 against 22.5% in the baseline.

banking_relevance.text: These are the only public measures of regulatory capital and liquidity, and they are more than half a year older than this month's banking data. The monthly book ratio of capital to assets, 12.5%, measures something different and is not a substitute.

caveat.text: Stress results are projections under an assumed scenario from the end-2025 exercise. They are not forecasts, not outcomes, and not a statement about any individual bank.

title.text: Lending grows 12.9% y/y to AZN 34.2 bn, with households contributing 7.8 pp and construction up 43.3%

interpretations.text: Loan growth of 12.9% is concentrated: households alone contribute 7.8 pp of it.
Construction lending is up 43.3% y/y, the fastest corporate segment, against non-oil activity growth of 2.1% year to date.
The published stock series cannot separate new origination from repayment, write-off and reclassification, so the composition question belongs to internal data.

so_what.text: Growth of this shape concentrates the book in households and one fast corporate segment; the sector limits that matter are the ones set before the concentration appears.

caveat.text: Sector loan growth is nominal and at current exchange rates.

title.text: Overdue balances rise AZN 194 mln y/y to 2.1% of loans while the bank NPL ratio holds near 2.9%

interpretations.text: The overdue ratio is 0.4 pp higher than a year ago at 2.1%, while the prudential NPL ratio rose only 0.1 pp to 2.9%.
The stability report put the sector NPL ratio at 3.3% at end-2025 on its own definition; the two measures are not interchangeable.
Portfolio growth flatters every ratio in this section: the denominator grew faster than the numerator in the last twelve months.

so_what.text: Watch the balances, not the ratios: the ratio is being held down by growth that will not continue at this pace indefinitely.

caveat.text: Overdue loans cover all credit institutions; the NPL series covers banks on prudential reporting. Neither identifies which borrowers moved.

title.text: Dollarisation keeps falling: the FX share of deposits is 34.7%, -3.5 pp lower than a year ago

interpretations.text: The FX share of all deposits fell 3.5 pp over the year to 34.7%; for households it is 28.1%.
Manat deposits are being priced up as this happens: the new AZN term deposit rate is 7.5%, 0.4 pp above a year ago.
A falling FX share reduces translation risk but raises the sensitivity of funding cost to the manat rate cycle.

so_what.text: Cheaper FX funding is leaving the system at the same time as manat deposits are repricing; the net effect on funding cost is a bank-specific question.

caveat.text: Shares are at current exchange rates and are not adjusted for revaluation.

title.text: Loan growth of 12.9% against deposit growth of 6.5% lifts the loan-to-deposit ratio to 76.8%

interpretations.text: The gap between loan and deposit growth is about six percentage points, and the loan-to-deposit ratio is 4.3 pp higher at 76.8%.
Household deposits grew 15.8% while corporate deposits fell 4.3%, so the funding mix is lengthening in one segment and shrinking in the other.
Deposits stand at AZN 44.5 bn against loans of AZN 34.2 bn.

so_what.text: If corporate balances keep falling, the marginal manat of funding is a priced retail deposit; that is an ALCO question about term and concentration, not only about rate.

caveat.text: A sector aggregate says nothing about any individual bank's liquidity position.

title.text: Rate held at 6.50% with the corridor at 5.50% to 7.50%, but the stated reasoning changed

interpretations.text: The corridor is unchanged at 5.50% to 7.50% with the refinancing rate at 6.50%.
The Bank states: \u201cRisks to the inflation outlook remain tilted to the upside\u201d.

quotes.text: Risks to the inflation outlook remain tilted to the upside

interpretations.text: An unchanged rate with a changed rationale narrows the range of outcomes that would leave policy where it is.

so_what.text: Treat the reasoning, not the level, as this month's new information for funding plans.

caveat.text: The stance label describes the rate decision only. No effective date is stated in the decision, so none is shown.

title.text: Inflation is 5.7% while the Bank's July round projects 6.1% at end-2026 and 5.8% at end-2027

interpretations.text: Actual inflation was 5.7% in August 2026; the projection for end-2026 is 6.1%.
The projection falls to 5.8% by end-2027, with non-oil growth of 2.4% this year.
Projections and outcomes are kept apart here; the chart shows outcomes only.

so_what.text: Planning assumptions that sit below the Bank's own projection need a stated reason.

caveat.text: Projections are the Central Bank's, published for named target periods and scenarios.

title.text: Sector capital adequacy 17.6% and liquidity coverage 154.0% at end-2025, published in April 2026

interpretations.text: Regulatory capital adequacy was 17.6% and the liquidity coverage ratio 154.0% at end-December 2025.
The monthly book ratio of capital to assets is 12.5% at end-July 2026 and measures something different.
Both dates are shown on every row because these measures are half-yearly and older than this month's banking data.

so_what.text: Use the regulatory measures for comparison with our own ratio, and the book measures for month-to-month movement; do not mix them.

caveat.text: Sector aggregates from the stability report; no bank-level distribution is published here.

title.text: The published adverse scenario takes sector capital adequacy to 13.6% by 2027 against 22.5% in the baseline

interpretations.text: Under the adverse scenario capital adequacy is projected at 13.6% by 2027; the baseline path reaches 22.5%.
The exercise starts from end-2025 data, when the actual ratio was 17.6%.
These are projections under an assumed shock, not forecasts and not losses that have occurred.

so_what.text: The scenario is public, so our own result on the same shocks is comparable evidence for the board; the sector path is the benchmark, not the answer.

caveat.text: Stress results carry their scenario and exercise date and are never presented as outcomes.

title.text: Net profit AZN 859 mln in January–July, up AZN 176 mln y/y, with annualised ROE at 19.5%

interpretations.text: Net profit reached AZN 859 mln year to date, AZN 176 mln more than a year earlier.
Annualised return on equity is 19.5%, close to the 18.2% the stability report published for end-2025.
Earnings at this level give the sector room to absorb higher impairment before capital is touched.

so_what.text: Current profitability is the buffer against the asset-quality drift on slide M10; that is the pair to watch together.

caveat.text: Prudential P&L, not IFRS. ROE annualises year-to-date profit over average month-end capital.

question.text: Is the sector-wide gap between loan growth of 12.9% and deposit growth of 6.5% visible in our own funding, and what is the plan if corporate balances keep falling?

signal.text: Loan-to-deposit ratio 76.8% (4.3 pp y/y); corporate deposits 4.3% lower.

why.text: Funding costs and liquidity buffers move first when deposit competition starts.

questions.internal_data: Own loan-to-deposit trend, deposit concentration, wholesale and FX funding lines, liquidity buffer against internal limits.
questions.watch: CBA deposits table 2.11 and rates table 3.2.1 for August 2026, expected by end-September.

question.text: Overdue balances are up AZN 194 mln y/y: are our early-arrears and roll rates moving the same way?

signal.text: Overdue ratio 2.1% (0.4 pp y/y) with the NPL ratio at 2.9%.

why.text: A ratio held down by portfolio growth can mask new formation; provisioning and underwriting decisions depend on the balances.

questions.internal_data: Vintage arrears, roll rates, restructured exposures and coverage by segment.
questions.watch: CBA NPL structure table 5.6 for August 2026; next monthly edition.

question.text: The Bank's July round projects 6.1% inflation at end-2026 while it holds the rate at 6.50%: what does our planning assume, and why?

signal.text: Actual inflation 5.7%; rate unchanged with a changed rationale.

why.text: Deposit repricing, lending demand and the real burden of existing debt all follow the inflation path.

questions.internal_data: Own inflation and rate assumptions in the plan, repricing gap, fixed-rate book written this year.
questions.watch: Next corridor decision on 23 September 2026 and the November review.
